transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Claire (Redwood SE), Olivia (CSM), Miguel (BlueArc CTO), Priya (Head of Platform), Jonas (SRE lead), Hannah (Product)

Summary: quick sync to align on recent SLA degradations, agree initial mitigation sprint, and hand off telemetry/artifacts for root-cause mini-experiment. Customer is worried about repeat long-tail latency spikes during peak pick/label workloads.

Topics: SLA regression timeline, KV cache behavior, autoscaler misconfiguration hypothesis, mitigation sprint scope, security/artifact handoff

Action items: (see metadata above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we know this is, like, a bit of a follow-up to the incident last week so we'll try to keep it focused. 
[00:12] Miguel (BlueArc): yeah thanks, appreciate it. we've had a couple of big customer complains, latency shot up during the 9am peak on 2027-01-09 and then again at 13:00. it wasn't constant but the long tail is what killed our SLA.
[00:25] Claire (Redwood SE): can you share what you mean by the long tail — is it request duration variance or token emission stalls?
[00:33] Miguel: mostly request duration, sometimes one out of 200 requests will jump to 7–10 seconds, where baseline is 200–400ms, and that knocks over our downstream pipelines.
[00:45] Priya (BlueArc): and a couple of them hit the dedicated pool we've got with Redwood Dedicated, so we thought capacity was reserved but it still had those spikes.
[00:54] Samir: yeah ok, quick confirmation — you're on Dedicated, pinned to the rdw-alpha-2 model, right?
[00:59] Miguel: yes rdw-alpha-2, pinned, dedicated pool of 6 GPUs.
[01:06] Claire: ok got it. initial hunches from our side: KV cache thrashing when sequence lengths vary, and autoscaler/backpressure interplay when a sudden burst forces rebalancing. Also some config with your ingress timeouts looked low, so occasionally requests were retrying and creating backpressure.
[01:30] Jonas (BlueArc): oh we did see retries. our HPA was set pretty aggressively — min 2, max 12 — but the ramp-up policy is slow, so you end up with lots of queued requests while pods start.
[01:45] Hannah (BlueArc): and I want to flag that our client SDK does optimistic retry on 504s which may have amplified the problem.
[01:52] Samir: that's a helpful detail. ok so the plan is we run two parallel tracks: telemetry/file handoff + small microbench experiments. Claire will run KV-cache microbench on a small repro, we will also examine your traces to identify the token-level hot-requests.
[02:10] Miguel: when you say KV-cache microbench, what does that look like?
[02:14] Claire: it mimics variable sequence lengths and prefix reuse; we instrument to see cache hit ratio and stall points. sometimes a single shard gets hot and the runtime moves to a fallback execution path that is slower. also quantization mismatches can change hot path.
[02:30] Priya: we've heard about quantization before — are you saying model variant/quantization could cause unpredictable latency?
[02:36] Claire: yeah in certain edge cases. not usually a huge effect, but combined with cache misses and dispatcher imbalance it can surface.
[02:44] Samir: worth noting too that our smart-routing may move some requests to a different node when a shard becomes overloaded — that adds network hop and KV rehydration.
[02:55] Miguel: hmm ok. quick question on security docs — we need to show our security team the data retention and audit logs before any internal pilot.
[03:04] Olivia (Redwood CSM): we will share the SOC2 excerpt and KMS integration notes; Samir will provide the sanitized traces without PII.
[03:13] Miguel: perfect.
[03:16] Jonas: do you have a recommended autoscaler config? our HPA seems to be part of the problem.
[03:21] Claire: based on what you've said, you might prefer slightly higher base capacity with faster scale-up (aggressive burst policy) and shorter liveness probes so new pods start handling traffic quicker. also enable prewarm/standby instances for critical windows.
[03:36] Priya: prewarm instances — is that something Redwood supports on Dedicated?
[03:39] Samir: yes, that's what we call reserved warm slots — you can keep a pool of warm actors ready to serve with minimal startup. it's a config on the Dedicated pool.
[03:49] Priya: ok that could help.
[03:51] Hannah: I also want to understand the economic tradeoffs — if we increase baseline capacity we'll pay more. what's the numbers?
[03:57] Samir: we'll get you a quick delta: cost for 2 warm spots vs current usage along with expected reduction in tail SLO violations. we'll model it and include it in the pilot scope doc.
[04:09] Miguel: another salvage question — are there fast fallbacks we can configure so if latency breaches X we return a cached summary rather than blocking downstream?
[04:18] Claire: yes, fallbacks can be configured: model variant fallback to a cheaper quantized model or response cache for certain prompt patterns. but that requires mapping which prompts are safe to approximate.
[04:29] Miguel: ok that sounds reasonable.
[04:31] [silence ~10s, participants check docs]
[04:45] Samir: let's go into artifacts — what we need from you is: 1) sanitized request traces for the windows 2027-01-09 09:00–10:30 and 13:00–14:00, 2) the HPA/autoscaler manifests, 3) your SDK retry policy.
[04:59] Priya: we can get those. we'll have someone sanitize first.
[05:03] Jonas: I'll export a pprof and a flamegraph for the 01-09 window.
[05:07] Claire: perfect. on our side we'll run the microbench and a quant-sensitivity test across a few sequence lengths. we might ask to reproduce a small sample of your workload if you can provide anonymized prompts.
[05:19] Miguel: about timeline, how fast can we get meaningful results?
[05:22] Claire: initial bench and trace review — 3 business days; pilot scope doc — 5 business days. so basically by next week.
[05:29] Hannah: makes sense. also, do you track token-level cost breakdowns per route? we need to show finance the potential uplift.
[05:36] Samir: yes Redwood Console has per-route token cost and latency breakdown — we'll attach screenshots and a sample export.
[05:44] Miguel: one more technical point — we saw a worker OOM on one pod during the incident, logs show a KV cache rehydration spike and then the process hit memory threshold. could that be the trigger?
[05:58] Claire: yep that's consistent with a hot shard scenario — rehydration can spike memory briefly. we'll verify in the microbench but plan for safe caps and hedged rehydration, plus optional memory-based circuit breaker.
[06:12] Priya: what would hedged rehydration look like?
[06:15] Claire: essentially staggered KV fetches and a short-lived local in-memory fallback so we avoid a single giant I/O hit. it adds complexity but stabilizes the tail.
[06:28] Miguel: ok interesting.
[06:30] Samir: quick risk/mitigation recap then: immediate—collect traces/logs and review autoscaler, medium—run KV microbench and enable prewarm warm slots, longer—pilot with slightly higher baseline and model-fallback rules.
[06:45] Jonas: for the pilot, what SLO uplift are we aiming to achieve?
[06:49] Samir: reasonable target: reduce 95th percentile by 30–40% and bring 99th under 2s for your peak traffic. we'll commit to measuring that.
[06:59] Miguel: that would be great.
[07:02] Hannah: any privacy concerns with traces? we need to be sure no PII leaks in the handoff.
[07:07] Olivia: we'll scrub at the field level and share a checklist of the sanitization steps we take; you can also run a secondary check before we ingest.
[07:16] Priya: ok thanks.
[07:18] Samir: a couple of practical notes — we'll open a shared folder and I'll drop a short readme with the minimum logs/fields we need. Claire will include a short bench harness repo link.
[07:30] Miguel: fine.
[07:32] [cross talk: someone muted/unmuted]
[07:40] Claire: quick technical nuance — when we talk about dispatcher fallback, sometimes transcription or the auto-caption in your console calls it 'K V cache thrash' and that phrase shows up in our old notes, so sorry if there's naming mismatch.
[07:52] Miguel: yes I saw K V cache in the logs, spelled like that.
[07:55] Claire: cool. we'll normalize naming in the doc.
[07:58] Samir: let's make sure the next sync is a short 30-minute alignment after you've shared artifacts. looking at calendars, week of 2027-01-25 works.
[08:09] Miguel: ok we'll aim for 2027-01-26.
[08:12] Samir: any other blockers?
[08:14] Hannah: just internal approvals for sending artifacts to Redwood security team — we'll expedite but may take 48hrs.
[08:20] Olivia: that's expected, we'll remain flexible.
[08:23] Miguel: also, curious what alternate vendors do — you mentioned Anthropic — did you mean they handle auto-scaling differently?
[08:30] Samir: different vendors have different routing fallbacks and some use more conservative batching which can reduce tail but increase average cost; we'll include comparative notes.
[08:42] Claire: also remember that some in-house self-hosted infra teams prefer to tune at the HPA layer rather than rely on warm pools. there's trade offs.
[08:51] Miguel: got it.
[08:53] Samir: ok final recap: next steps and action items in the repo, Claire runs the bench and shares findings, Samir shares sanitized traces and cost/latency export, Olivia shares SOC2 excerpt and KMS notes, customer provides manifests and pprof snapshots. Aim for follow-up 2027-01-26 to review pilot scope.
[09:12] Miguel: thanks everyone.
[09:14] Priya: thanks.
[09:16] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-caption had some minor mislabels (Speaker 1), occasional transcript artifacts (K V cache vs KV-cache), and a few filler words left in — overall medium quality.
